title: LP2 grid as an OpenPGP literal packet?
question: Does the LP2-49–51 base-60 grid form one complete OpenPGP literal-data packet at byte zero under fixed rectangular readings and disputed I/L stems?
summary: The printed-order stream starts with the literal-data tag CB, but no complete literal-data packet appears among 16,384 fixed grid readings.
finding: Of 16,384 fixed readings, 4,096 begin with CB but fail complete-packet framing because bytes remain after the encoded length; 12,288 do not begin with the literal-data tag. No reading is one complete tag-11 packet.
limitations: Only one untransformed new-format OpenPGP tag-11 packet occupying all 256 bytes at offset zero is tested. This does not reject embedded packets, multi-packet messages, other routes, other glyph choices, encryption or transformed bytes.
next_steps: A further OpenPGP proposal must state its packet offset, byte transformation and whether multiple packets are permitted, then supply a complete parse with independently checked controls.

scope.representation: 256 printed grid tokens as bytes under the declared base-60 digit order; ten disputed I/L cells have two allowed readings.
scope.procedure: Enumerate 16 row/column routes and 1,024 stem masks; check complete RFC 4880 new-format tag-11 packet framing at offset zero with definite and partial lengths and literal body fields.
scope.parameters: 16,384 byte streams; each 256 bytes. Valid tag11 header CB; packet must consume entire stream. Two planted packet controls including partial-length encoding.
scope.exclusions: Other OpenPGP packet tags, streams of multiple packets, nonzero offsets, transformed data, 16×16 layout, other base/digit orders and unregistered glyph readings.

review.reviewer: Deterministic byte parser with planted packets

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; input grid and stem-results files from the reference-data bundle.

visuals.caption: The 4,096 tag starts fail packet framing; no complete literal-data packet is present.

sources.label: RFC 4880 OpenPGP packet lengths and literal data

reader_note: The first byte can resemble an OpenPGP tag; complete packet framing fails.
reader_limit: This excludes only one complete untransformed literal-data packet at byte zero.
